raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, and my family has people working outside, so I will not spread myself too thin on labor-heavy crops. I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady part of the farm here, and I have well water, so I can hold yield if the sky does not help. Cotton I will still plant, but only on a small piece, because cotton eats more labor and more sprays. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer.

What I will do is close to what I know works around Quzhou, not the very high-input demo-field way. On the wheat-maize land, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, with fertilizer a little on the safe side because the land has to carry two crops in one year. Wheat I will water about 3 times if needed: once before winter or at overwintering, once at jointing, once at filling. Maize I will water 2 times, mainly at big bell and grain filling. Cotton I will keep on 1 mu with hybrid seed, one base fertilizer shot and then topdress later, and I will watch insects closely because if aphids, bollworm, or mites rise, cotton can turn bad fast. With my small area, I will choose simple operations that save labor: rotary for wheat ground, no-tillage maize after wheat, and plough once for cotton ground so the field is cleaner and easier to manage.
